risks.title: Unverified ICE roundup rumors causing panic
risks.description: January 2025 social posts reported mass raids in Pueblo; CPR confirmed the incident involved ICE assisting a narcotics arrest, but fear persisted and door-knock claims spread statewide.
risks.impact: Can trigger unnecessary school/work absences, hamper reporting, and obscure real enforcement actions.
recommended_actions: Verify sightings through CORRN hotline before sharing.
Issue clarifying messages when rumors are debunked.
Maintain rapid logging (time, location, vehicles) for confirmed operations.

policies.title: Pueblo County Sheriff cooperation limits
policies.summary: Sheriff David Lucero pledged PCSO will not help ICE with civil 'round-up' operations and will only participate when there are criminal charges or officer-safety concerns.
policies.implications: Provides a documented commitment to cite if deputies assist immigration enforcement absent criminal nexus.
actions: Carry copies of the statement at protests, schools, and clinics.
Log any deviations for escalation to POST/AG Pattern & Practice.
sources: Pueblo County Sheriff’s Office news release, 2025-01-23

resources.name: Colorado Rapid Response Network (CORRN)
services: Statewide hotline 844-864-8341 (option 1 for live raids, option 2 for past incidents)
Dispatch of trained legal observers and documentation teams
Data sharing with Colorado Immigrant Rights Coalition organizers
resources.notes: Program hotline into protest/legal observer phones; pair reports with badges, vehicle info, and timestamps.

resources.name: Rocky Mountain Immigrant Advocacy Network (RMIAN)
services: Legal orientation and direct representation for detained adults at Aurora GEO
Child advocacy program for unaccompanied minors
Social service support for released families
resources.notes: Collect A-numbers, detention location, and contact info before calling; Pueblo families can request phone consults.

resources.name: Colorado Immigrant Rights Coalition (CIRC)
services: Volunteer training for hotline response and accompaniment
Know-your-rights materials tailored to Colorado communities
resources.notes: Pueblo organizers can join statewide alerts and mobilize local volunteers to support CORRN dispatches and legislative pushes.
